Engineered to the last degree.

GE6° is Neural Drift’s voyage-intelligence engine. One core plans the passage, keeps the watch and audits the outcome, so ship and shore act on the same truth at the same moment.

  1. NEXTVoyage PlannerOptimization before departure
  2. NOWLive WatchkeeperVigilance at sea, every hour
  3. PASTVoyage AnalysisThe truth after arrival

Read the ring clockwise: plan before departure, keep the watch at sea, analyse after arrival. Every voyage sharpens the next.

A superintendent with superintelligence.

GE6° was built for the people who answer for a ship’s performance: technical superintendents, commercial operators, charterers, and the Masters who carry those decisions to sea.

It fuses eight living streams of maritime data into one continuously reconciled model of the voyage, and speaks through three disciplined services. Before departure it optimizes the passage. At sea it keeps the watch. After arrival it states, without flattery, how the ship truly performed, then carries every lesson into the next plan.

The result is a closed loop of navigational intelligence that grows sharper with every mile sailed.

Eight streams. One reconciled truth.

Weather, currents, position, noon reports, charter terms, bunkers, sea-trial signatures and port regulation arrive at different speeds, in different formats and with different degrees of certainty. GE6° validates and reconciles every one of them before a single recommendation is made, because an engine is only as honest as the evidence it is fed.

Three services. One unbroken loop.

Each service owns a sector of the ring and a moment in the life of a voyage. What is learned after arrival shapes what is planned before the next departure.

SV·01Before departure285°–045°

Voyage Planner

Optimization, before the first waypoint is laid.

Voyage Planner resolves the passage that best balances safety, schedule, fuel and carbon intensity. Forecast weather, ocean currents, emission control areas, port constraints and the charter party’s warranted terms are weighed together, not in sequence, and the result is a plan the Master can interrogate, amend and own.

“We suggest this course after our models have run their calculations under the ethical considerations of high-frequency econometrics.”

  • Alternative passages compared side by side, including the Master’s own route
  • Weather and current exposure flagged day by day
  • Fuel planned by grade, with remaining on board at arrival
  • Emission control areas and fuel changeovers prepared in advance
  • Charter-party terms honoured from the first waypoint
  • Routes exported for the bridge in RTZ format
Open Voyage Planner

SV·02Live at sea045°–165°

Live Watchkeeper

A second watch that never stands down.

From the moment the vessel sails, Live Watchkeeper holds the voyage under continuous observation. Live position, weather and sea state are reconciled against the agreed plan, deviation is detected as it emerges, and recovery or evasive alternatives are proposed before cost or risk can compound.

“Routes that are unsafe for the hull, or impossible for her draught, are discarded before they can ever be displayed.”

  • Plan-versus-track reconciliation, around the clock
  • Early warning the moment a voyage drifts from its plan
  • Weather-evasive and schedule-recovery alternatives
  • The charter-compliant route held as the default
  • Alerts to ship and shore at the same moment
  • The Master’s own route, checkable at any hour
Open Live Watchkeeper

SV·03After arrival165°–285°

Voyage Analysis

The unvarnished truth, after arrival.

Voyage Analysis reconstructs how the ship genuinely performed, leg by leg, from commencement to end of sea passage. Speed and fuel are measured against her own sea-trial baseline and against the charter party’s warranted terms on the days that qualify. Every deviation is isolated, quantified and handed back to the next plan.

“Evidence composed to hold its ground in the most demanding commercial conversation.”

  • Leg-by-leg performance, sea passage or port to port
  • Speed and fuel deviation against the sea-trial baseline
  • Charter-party speed and consumption, verified on qualifying days
  • Findings in one clear table and two deviation graphs
  • Carbon intensity (CII) read in its operational context
  • Calculated on demand, for the voyage you select
Open Voyage Analysis

How GE6° decides.

Capability without discipline is noise. These are the rules the engine keeps, without exception.

We suggest. The Master decides.

GE6° is decision intelligence, never an autopilot. Every recommendation arrives with its reasoning, and the Master’s overriding authority under SOLAS V/34-1 is never diluted.

Calculated under ethical constraint.

Our models observe the ethical considerations of high-frequency econometrics: no signal is over-fitted, no uncertainty is concealed, and no economy is pursued at the expense of safety.

A reading is never rewritten.

Implausible values are questioned and flagged, never silently corrected. Altering an operator’s measurement would invent data, and invented data has no place aboard.

Provenance in every figure.

Each number traces back to the stream that produced it, from the bunker delivery note to the noon report it came from.

One voyage, one truth.

Ship and shore read the same model at the same moment, in the same language. Reconciliation happens inside the engine, not in a spreadsheet after the fact.

Compliance, designed in.

Carbon intensity, emission control areas and charter obligations are woven into planning and analysis from the first calculation, never bolted on afterwards.

Lighter on the ocean.

Shipping carries most of the world’s trade, and every passage leaves a trace in the air and in the water. GE6° exists to make that trace smaller, with arithmetic rather than slogans.

That is why GE6° treats fuel as carbon. Every tonne the engine helps a ship avoid keeps roughly three tonnes of CO2 out of the sky.

Fuel is carbon.

The cleanest tonne of fuel is the one never burned. Route, speed and weather optimization cut consumption at its source, before a single gram is emitted.

Arrive when you are expected.

Voyage Planner paces the passage to the arrival that is actually required, not the fastest one possible, so ships stop racing across oceans only to idle at anchor.

Carbon intensity, in context.

CII is read voyage by voyage beside the weather, currents and cargo that shaped it, so improvement plans address causes instead of symptoms.

Counted from what was truly bunkered.

Emissions follow the grade on each bunker delivery note and the conversion factor that grade demands, never a fleet-wide assumption that flatters the result.

Cleaner hulls, cleaner seas.

Deviation from the sea-trial baseline shows when hull and propeller start costing fuel. A clean hull burns less and stops carrying invasive species between ecosystems.

No greenwashing.

We never round a ship greener than she is. Deviations are reported exactly as measured, because honest numbers are the only foundation for real reduction.

Conceived at sea. Engineered in India.

GE6° is engineered by seafarers: marine engineers who have stood engine-room watches on tankers and carried a running plant through the night. Every screen is held to the standard of the bridge and the engine room. If it would not survive a night watch in heavy weather, it does not ship.
